feeds.title: WEA Pedagogy Blog
feeds.description: The WEA Pedagogy Platform is an open forum for the exchange of ideas from anyone interested in contributing. This Platform is aimed at stimulating the interdisciplinary transfer of knowledge, cross-pollination between diverse ideas, and constructive dialogue.

feeds.title: Speakeasy News » Pedagogy
feeds.description: Speakeasy News brings the news to the heart of English teaching. Let the English-speaking world into your classroom with regular news updates. The latest politics and events, festivals and festivities, cultural commemorations, films, books, exhibitions and theatre in the English-speaking world, on the web and in France. In Pedagogy, you will find articles on teaching practice, and information about educational reforms, competitions and projects.

feeds.title: Pedagogy Before Technology
feeds.description: Dr. Gloria Washington is an instructional designer at the Center for Teaching Excellence (CTE) with 23 years of experience in higher education at the University of South Carolina. She is a Blackboard Certified Trainer and a Blackboard Exemplary Course Program Reviewer. Her blog Pedagogy Before Technology is a peer-reviewed and research-based academic blog about pedagogy.

feeds.title: Education, Pedagogy & Formation Blog
feeds.description: This blog has been written for a specialised audience. It is essentially a guide for teachers, university students, clergy and parents that considers pedagogy and education from a Christian perspective. However, while I write as a Christian to address people who share the Christian faith, I believe that much of what I have to say is just as relevant for people of other faiths. I am Trevor Cairney - a Professor of Education at The University of Sydney, Australia. I have spent a large part of my adult life as a teacher, academic, researcher and senior university administrator.

feeds.title: All Things Pedagogical
feeds.description: A blog about how and why we teach, including pedagogical ethics and instructional technology. I am Ann, an Educational Developer passionate about access and ethical pedagogy. I support the use of Universal Design for Learning in framing engaging and multimodal teaching and learning.

feeds.title: Persistence and Pedagogy
feeds.description: I'm a high school English and Social Science teacher in Ottawa, Ontario. I'm also a reader, a writer, a walker, a partner and a mother of two. I use this space to think and write about teaching and living.

feeds.title: Early Childhood Pedagogy Network Blog
feeds.description: As part of the ECPN commitment to creating a lively platform for critical reflection and discussion, this blog offers brief posts that address a wide range of topics relevant to early childhood pedagogy. The ECPN is the provincial group of pedagogists who support early childhood educators in BC.

feeds.title: ThemPra Social Pedagogy News
feeds.description: Our website offers an insight into the theory and practice of social pedagogy. We outline why we believe social pedagogy can make a positive difference and what we at ThemPra do to make this become reality. ThemPra is a social (pedagogical) enterprise supporting the sustainable development of social pedagogy.

feeds.title: Letters and Ink Blog » Pedagogy
feeds.description: This is your home for strategies and resources to empower you to teach for equity and teach for justice. I'm Luci, the creator of Letters and Ink! I created the Letters and Ink Blog first as a place to share my philosophy because I was constantly gaslit and shut down by my colleagues and administration when I tried to advocate for my students. Now, it serves as validation for the thousands of teachers who experience the same pushback when you fight for your students.

feeds.title: Funky Pedagogy Blog
feeds.description: Jennifer Webb's English Teachers blog covering classroom strategies, resources and reflections in literature, language, grammar & more.

feeds.title: TESL Ontario Blog » Pedagogy
feeds.description: Learn more about our teaching models, tips, English teaching and more! The TESL Ontario Blog Project was created because of the TESL Ontario members' strong community engagement. In 2013, members made it known that they wished to have a forum to share resources and learn from others' experiences. Since 2014, we've been making it happen.

feeds.title: Data Pedagogy
feeds.description: Thoughts longer than a tweet, shorter than a manuscript on data, pedagogy, and data pedagogy. My name is Mine Dogucu and I teach statistics and data science. I spend a good chunk of my time thinking about how to be a better data scientist, teacher, and human. I created this blog to share what is going on in my mind and in my classes.

feeds.title: The PlanBee Blog » Pedagogy
feeds.description: Articles and advice for primary educators, homeschool parents and school leaders - all written by the PlanBee team of experienced teachers. PlanBee is the hive of lesson planning and primary resources for schools and teachers. We're a small team of former teachers, dedicated to creating exciting, ready-to-teach lesson planning packs that save teachers time.

feeds.title: Paper, Pens and Pedagogy Blog
feeds.description: I am Christina McGhie. I trained with Teach First in 2006, and have taught in London, Yorkshire and Teesside. I love all things pedagogy and think that we have a lot to learn from the cognitive science of learning, that could be effectively implemented in our classrooms. In my blog, I present my perspective on a range of matters from my experience as a Science teacher and leader.

feeds.title: Fiona Saunders » Pedagogy Blogs
feeds.description: I am Faculty Director of Education in the Faculty of Science and Engineering at Manchester Metropolitan University and Professor of Project Management Education. I lead on all aspects of the Education Strategy from teaching and learning to employability. Explore the pedagogy blog articles to know more about the teaching method, resources and more!

feeds.title: Transcending Pedagogy Blog
feeds.description: Read about my in-real-life classroom teaching experiences, planning for diverse learners, the joys and frustrations that are inherent in teaching, specific plans and ideas to stimulate reading, writing, and thinking, the constant revisioning and rethinking that is the hallmark of great teaching and leading, and the real-time changes, adaptations, successes and failures that happen daily in the work. Transcending Pedagogy is a space devoted to helping educators grow as inspiring, creative, and reflective teachers, and as open-minded and evolving learners.

feeds.title: Pedagogy to Share
feeds.description: Pedagogy to Share is a blog that will follow and record my learning and my practice as a teacher-educator. My name is Nikki Aharonian, and I am an Australian-born lecturer in the Faculty of Education and the Department of English Language and Literature at the Oranim College of Education in Israel. My research interests include writing, writing pedagogy, narrative, dialogic education, and professional learning.

feeds.title: Achieve the Core
feeds.description: Achieve the Core's Peers and Pedagogy is a publication dedicated to high-quality instructional materials and their use in classrooms. Peers and Pedagogy is a space for educators and those who support educators to share experiences, ideas, best practices, and challenges around what it means to ensure all students thrive academically and emotionally. The blog specifically focuses on supporting students' learning through equitable classroom practice, instructional materials, and professional learning and interpersonal connections.

feeds.title: Maitri Learning Blog » Pedagogy
feeds.description: Maitri Learning was founded somewhat accidentally by a Montessori teacher who was trying to buy the perfect materials for her classroom and couldn't find them anywhere. Now, the materials she created (based specifically on the precise directions received in her AMI training) are used by Montessori teachers, parents, and teacher trainers around the world.

feeds.title: UoE Education Incubator Blog
feeds.description: On the Education Incubator Blog we share the views and opinions of our fellows and students; with updates about their experiences, projects, and initiatives, and other content related to innovation, pedagogy, and University-wide issues. This blog is the companion of the Education Incubator website, where you can find further details about our projects, events, and future funding opportunities.

feeds.title: TeachThought » Pedagogy
feeds.description: Explore research, learning models, teaching strategies, research on learning, resource collections, how-to guides, clarifying definitions, inspirational quotes, and more on Pedagogy. Terry Heick was a classroom teacher before founding TeachThought in 2010, an organization dedicated to humanizing education through a combination of creative innovation, and sustainable, research-based practice.
